input: What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?

output.question: What guidance did Nike give for the current quarter on its most recent earnings call, and how did the stock react?
output.answer: Nike gave no formal revenue or margin forecast for the current quarter (fiscal Q2 FY27, roughly September to November 2026) on its October 1, 2026 call for fiscal Q1 FY27. CFO Dave Denton said Nike will give a full-year view and update it as the year goes on. For Q2 he only pointed to about 400 basis points of revenue headwind from two things: last year's heavy Cyber Week discounting in EMEA and last year's higher North America sell-in. He also said Q2 growth and gross margin would be under pressure. For the full year, Nike expects revenue to fall by a high-single-digit percentage and EBIT to fall faster than revenue, with adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35. That range excludes about $0.15 of cost from the new 'Pace' restructuring program and sits below consensus estimates of about $1.61 to $1.66. The shares fell about 3% in after-hours trading on October 1, even though Q1 EPS of $0.48 beat the $0.43 estimate (revenue was $11.21B, down 4%, a miss). On Friday, October 2, the stock traded down about 5.3% intraday at $33.29, from a $35.15 close the day before, with a session low of $31.97.

key_facts.fact: Nike held its Q1 FY27 earnings call on October 1, 2026 and gave no quarterly guidance. The CFO said Nike intends to 'provide a view of our expectations for the full fiscal year and update that perspective as the year progresses.'
For Q2, the CFO named two items, lapping significant EMEA Cyber Week promotions and a higher North America sell-in comparison, as a revenue headwind of about 400 basis points.

FY27 guidance: revenue down by a high-single-digit percentage, EBIT down by a larger percentage than revenue, SG&A down year over year, and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.35 excluding about $0.15 of Pace program impact. The outlook assumes China gets worse for the rest of the year.
Q1 FY27 results: EPS of $0.48 vs. $0.43 expected; revenue of $11.21B, down 4%, vs. $11.32B expected; Greater China revenue down 26%. Shares fell about 3% in extended trading.
On Friday, October 2, 2026, NKE traded down 5.28% at $33.29 from a $35.15 prior close, with an intraday range of $31.97 to $33.37 on about 57.6M shares.
Tiger Brokers reported Nike fell 8.19% overnight to $32.10.

caveats: Nike gave no formal revenue, gross-margin or EPS range for Q2 FY27. The only Q2-specific number was the roughly 400bp revenue headwind, plus a qualitative note that Q2 growth and margins would be pressured.
The tools I used return summarized transcript text, so the quotes may be slightly trimmed. Check exact wording against the full transcript on investors.nike.com.

I could not confirm the official October 2, 2026 closing price. Reports conflict: one says down 5.28% at $33.29 intraday, another says down 8.19% overnight at $32.10, which is likely an extended or overnight-session price.
Consensus figures for FY27 EPS vary by source ($1.61 from Yahoo/StockTitan coverage, $1.66 in other reports).
Nike's fiscal Q2 FY27 results, likely due in mid-to-late December 2026, will replace this information. One report says the full-year outlook could be revised at an Investor Day or with Q2 results.
